posts.excerpt: Electromagnetic Transduction Therapy (EMTT)In Brooklyn, New York Knee pain is a common problem in people over 50 years of age. As we grow older, the cartilage between the joints starts to deteriorate. In some cases, it is also caused due to an injury or trauma. Even being overweight or obese can cause the cartilage to […]
posts.content:
Electromagnetic Transduction Therapy (EMTT)
In Brooklyn, New York

Knee pain is a common problem in people over 50 years of age. As we grow older, the cartilage between the joints starts to deteriorate. In some cases, it is also caused due to an injury or trauma. Even being overweight or obese can cause the cartilage to deteriorate. This causes the bones to rub or grind against each other, resulting in immense pain, swelling, and inflammation. This is also known as knee osteoarthritis.

The cartilage acts as a cushion between the joints. Once the cartilage starts to deteriorate, there isn’t much you can do about it apart from surgery. Knee replacement surgery uses knee implants and may take months to heal. This is where the best pain management specialist near me will suggest knee gel injections.

Gel injections for arthritic knees are a great alternative pain management treatment. This is your last resort before your doctor recommends you to get under the knife.

This post covers what you need to know about knee pain, from what causes it to what the treatment options actually are.

What Causes Knee Pain?

There are several reasons why an individual may suffer from knee osteoarthritis. Osteoarthritis (OA) is the most common form of arthritis and one of the leading causes of disability. Nevertheless, the most common cause is age.

As you age, your body’s ability to heal quickly is compromised. So, it takes significantly greater time to heal the cartilage in an older person. Irrespective of that, almost everyone, at some point in their life, will develop some degree of osteoarthritis. But, there are several factors that increase the risk of developing knee osteoarthritis at an early age. They include:

  • Weight: As you gain weight, it increases the pressure on your knee joints. Since the primary role of your knee is to support your upper body, for every pound you gain, it will be adding 3-4 pounds of extra weight on your knees. This drastically affects the cartilage between the knee joints. And with constant activities that involve knee movement, the cartilage deteriorates. 
  • Athletics: If you are involved in some kind of sports like soccer, football, basketball, etc. then you are at a higher risk of developing knee problems. When you jump, sprint, and perform other sports activities that put pressure on your knees, the cartilage can get damaged. Thus, you need to take proper precautions as well as take care of your nutrition.
  • Repetitive Stress Injuries: Those who lift weights are prone to these injuries. Also, these injuries are a result of the type of jobs people do. Any activity that involves stressing the joints can cause knee osteoarthritis.
  • Family History: If someone in your family has knee problems, then you are likely to get one. The inherited abnormalities can cause the knee joints to degrade over time.
  • Other Diseases: People with metabolic disorders like excess growth hormone or iron overload run the risk of knee osteoarthritis. Also, people with rheumatoid arthritis can also get osteoarthritis.

Knee Gel Injections for Knee Pain

Your pain management specialist may suggest injections as a treatment for knee pain. The gel injections for arthritic knees take up the role of the cartilage. Since the cartilage between the joints prevents the bones from grinding, the gel injection works similarly. It is injected directly into the knee joint to provide immediate relief. While there are several different types of knee gel injections available, doctors prefer corticosteroid injections.

Recently, Duke University researchers said that they’ve created an experimental gel that’s the first to match the strength and durability of cartilage. The team says eventually the research could offer new options for people with knee pain.

What are corticosteroid injections?

Corticosteroid is a drug that is designed to act the same way as the natural cortisol hormone produced by the body. Cortisol is responsible for working with the immune system to reduce inflammation and relieve pain.

The FDA has approved five different knee gel injections to treat knee pain. You should read the approved knee gel injection reviews so that you can make an informed decision. The gel injection for knee pain is performed with the help of ultrasound as it helps in locating the exact spot where the needle must be inserted.

It is a minimally invasive procedure, and the doctor may give you an injection of anesthetic pain relief along with the gel injection.

Please note that steroid injections are only for pain management. That is, it only provides temporary pain relief. For effective pain management, appropriate rehabilitation is also necessary.

Frequently asked questions

How is EMTT different from shockwave therapy?
They use different forms of energy. Shockwave sends acoustic pressure waves into tissue through a handpiece pressed against the skin, while electromagnetic transduction therapy uses a high-energy magnetic field produced by an applicator positioned over the area. They are sometimes used within the same treatment plan, because they are not interchangeable.

Is EMTT applied to the knee itself or over a wider area?
Usually over a wider area than the sore spot. The applicator produces a field that covers a region rather than a point, so the joint and the surrounding muscle and tendon are treated together, and positioning is chosen to include the structures thought to be involved. That is different from a handpiece worked directly over one tender area.

Can EMTT be used alongside knee gel injections?
Often yes, since they act on different things. An injection works inside the joint, while EMTT is applied from outside and targets the surrounding tissue, so a plan sometimes includes both, spaced out rather than given on the same day. Timing is worth confirming with whoever performed the injection.

Is EMTT used for anything besides knee arthritis?
Yes. It is applied to a range of musculoskeletal problems, including back, shoulder, hip and tendon pain, and it is generally one part of a broader plan rather than a stand-alone treatment. Whether it suits a particular problem depends on the diagnosis, which is why an evaluation comes before any course of treatment.

Wondering whether EMTT applies to your condition?

A physician-led evaluation matches the technology to the diagnosis. More on EMTT therapy.

posts.title: TECAR Therapy: What It Is and How It Works
posts.excerpt: If you’re researching pain treatment options in Brooklyn, you may have come across TECAR therapy and wondered what it actually involves. TECAR stands for Transfer of Energy Capacitive and Resistive, a non-invasive treatment that uses radiofrequency energy to generate heat inside the body’s own tissue, rather than applying heat from the outside. A plain explanation […]
posts.content:
If you’re researching pain treatment options in Brooklyn, you may have come across TECAR therapy and wondered what it actually involves. TECAR stands for Transfer of Energy Capacitive and Resistive, a non-invasive treatment that uses radiofrequency energy to generate heat inside the body’s own tissue, rather than applying heat from the outside. A plain explanation of the technology is in TECAR therapy explained.

How TECAR Therapy Works

During a TECAR session, a handheld electrode is moved across the skin while a return electrode completes the circuit. The device delivers a radiofrequency current that passes through the tissue, and the body’s own resistance to that current generates heat at a cellular level. This is different from a heating pad or hot pack, which only warms the surface of the skin. Because the heat is generated deeper in the muscle, tendon, or joint tissue, TECAR is often used to target structures that are harder to reach with surface-level treatments.

Practitioners typically alternate between two modes: a capacitive mode, which is gentler and works well on more superficial soft tissue, and a resistive mode, which concentrates energy more precisely and is often used on denser tissue like tendons, ligaments, and areas closer to bone.

What TECAR Is Used For

TECAR therapy is commonly used as part of a broader treatment plan for muscle strains, tendon irritation, joint stiffness, and general chronic pain conditions. It’s frequently paired with physical therapy, since the increased blood flow and tissue temperature can make a joint or muscle group more receptive to stretching and strengthening work that follows. How it applies to chronic injury is set out in TECAR therapy for chronic injuries.

Patients who are looking for non-surgical, drug-free options, or who want to reduce their reliance on oral pain medication, often ask about TECAR as part of a multi-modal approach that may also include laser therapy, targeted injections, or manual therapy, depending on the diagnosis.

What to Expect During a Session

A typical TECAR session runs between fifteen and thirty minutes. Most patients describe the sensation as a comfortable, gradually building warmth rather than any kind of shock or discomfort. TECAR is generally well tolerated, and side effects are uncommon, though as with any treatment, your provider will review your history to confirm you’re a good candidate before starting.

Is TECAR Right for You?

TECAR isn’t a fit for every condition, and it works best as one part of a coordinated plan rather than a stand-alone fix. Individual results vary, and TECAR is not guaranteed to eliminate pain on its own. The best way to know whether it makes sense for your specific situation is a proper evaluation with a provider who can look at your full history and current symptoms.

If you’re in Brooklyn and want to talk through whether TECAR therapy fits your treatment plan, a pain management provider can walk you through the available options.

Frequently asked questions

Can TECAR be used over a metal implant or a joint replacement?
Not without checking first. TECAR passes a radiofrequency current through tissue, and metal implants, pacemakers and other electronic devices change how that energy behaves, so they are screened for beforehand. Some situations rule the treatment out entirely, while others only change where the electrodes are placed, which is a decision for the provider.

Can TECAR be used on the neck or close to the head?
The neck is treated in some plans, but the closer the area is to the head, the more cautious the setup becomes. Treatment over the eyes, the front of the throat and directly over the skull is generally avoided, and settings are kept lower in that region. Anyone with an implanted device in the head or neck is screened first.

Can TECAR burn the skin?
It should not. The device is designed to produce heat within the tissue rather than at the surface, and the electrode is kept moving with a conductive cream, which is why the sensation is a building warmth rather than a hot spot. Saying immediately if any point feels sharp or too hot keeps the setting in a safe range.

Is TECAR safe when an area feels numb or has reduced sensation?
It calls for extra caution. Heat-based treatment relies partly on the person reporting when warmth becomes too much, and that warning is missing where sensation is reduced by nerve damage, diabetes-related neuropathy or scarring. Lower settings, shorter times, or a treatment that does not depend on heat may be chosen instead after assessment.

Wondering whether TECAR therapy applies to your pain?

Do arthritic knees really hurt more in cold or damp weather?

posts.title: What Doctor Should You See for Knee Pain or Leg Pain?
posts.excerpt: TL;DR For most knee or leg pain, start with your primary care doctor or a pain management doctor. The right specialist depends on the cause. Knee pain from arthritis, overuse or an old injury: pain management, physical medicine or orthopedics. A new injury with swelling or a knee that gives way: orthopedics or sports medicine. […]
posts.content:
TL;DR

For most knee or leg pain, start with your primary care doctor or a pain management doctor. The right specialist depends on the cause.

  • Knee pain from arthritis, overuse or an old injury: pain management, physical medicine or orthopedics.
  • A new injury with swelling or a knee that gives way: orthopedics or sports medicine.
  • Leg pain with numbness, tingling or shooting pain: pain management or neurology (often a nerve from the back).
  • Leg pain when walking that eases with rest: a vascular doctor. A swollen, warm, painful calf: same-day care.
  • Several swollen joints at once: rheumatology.

What doctor should you see for knee pain?

Most people with knee pain can start with a primary care doctor or a pain management doctor. Both can examine the knee, order X-rays or an MRI and start treatment. Which specialist is best depends on what is causing the pain:

Knee problem Doctor to consider
Arthritis, stiffness, pain with stairs Pain management, physical medicine (physiatry), orthopedics
Sudden injury, popping, swelling within hours, knee gives way Orthopedics or sports medicine
Pain in the front of the knee from running or squatting Sports medicine, physical therapy, pain management
Swelling that keeps coming back Pain management, rheumatology, orthopedics
Several joints swollen at once, morning stiffness over an hour Rheumatology
Pain that continues after knee replacement The surgeon first, then pain management

Related: knee osteoarthritis, pain in the front of the knee, fluid on the knee (CR-1, link once live).

What doctor should you see for leg pain?

The right doctor for leg pain depends on whether it comes from a nerve, a muscle, a joint or a blood vessel:

Leg pain pattern Doctor to consider
Shooting, burning or electric pain from the back or buttock down the leg Pain management, neurology, spine specialist
Numbness or burning in both feet Primary care first (blood sugar, B12), then neurology or pain management
Cramping in the calf when walking that stops with rest Vascular doctor
Aching, heavy legs with visible veins or ankle swelling Vascular doctor
Muscle strain or pain after exercise Primary care, sports medicine, physical therapy

See leg pain causes: nerve, muscle, vein or artery and sciatica.

What does a pain management doctor do for knee and leg pain?

A pain management doctor diagnoses the source of pain and treats it without surgery. That can include physical therapy plans, injections such as steroid or gel (hyaluronic acid) injections, nerve-focused treatments and technology-based therapies. Pain management is a good fit when pain has lasted weeks or months, keeps coming back, or when you want to avoid or delay surgery. See knee pain treatment without surgery.

When should you see an orthopedic surgeon instead?

See an orthopedic surgeon when an injury may need repair or when non-surgical care has not helped. Signs include a knee that locks or gives way, a suspected ligament tear, a fracture, or advanced arthritis that limits daily life despite treatment.

When is knee or leg pain an emergency?

Go to the ER or call 911 for: – A swollen, warm, red or painful calf, especially after travel, surgery or bed rest (possible blood clot) – Leg pain with shortness of breath or chest pain – A leg that is cold, pale or numb – A knee that is hot and red with fever – Being unable to bear weight after a fall or injury

See leg pain: doctor, urgent care or the ER.

Do you need a referral to see a specialist?

It depends on your insurance plan. Original Medicare and most PPO plans do not require referrals; many HMO and Medicaid managed care plans do. See do you need a referral for pain management in New York (CR-2, link once live).

Frequently asked questions

Should I see an orthopedist or a pain management doctor for knee pain?

For arthritis, overuse or long-lasting pain, either can help; pain management focuses on non-surgical care. For a new injury that may need repair, start with orthopedics.

Can a primary care doctor treat knee pain?

Yes. Many cases of mild knee pain are evaluated and treated in primary care, with a referral to a specialist if needed.

What kind of doctor treats knee and leg pain at the same time?

A pain management or physical medicine doctor often evaluates both, especially when a nerve or the hip is involved.

Can hip problems cause knee pain?

Yes. Hip arthritis and nerve irritation can be felt in the knee. See [could your hip be causing your knee pain?](https://paintherapycare.com/blog/hip-causing-knee-pain-brooklyn/)

Do I need an MRI before seeing a specialist?

Usually not. The doctor decides whether imaging is needed after examining you. See [MRI for knee pain](https://paintherapycare.com/blog/mri-for-knee-pain-brooklyn/).

What doctor treats leg pain from the back?

Pain management, physical medicine and spine specialists commonly treat leg pain caused by a pinched nerve in the lower back.

posts.title: Why do knees hurt when running?
posts.excerpt: Whether you have just started running as part of your new workout regime or are a seasoned veteran who has been running for years, the chances are that you may have experienced a bit of pain in the knee. This is called runner’s knee. Running is a high-impact activity that puts loads of stress on […]
posts.content:
Whether you have just started running as part of your new workout regime or are a seasoned veteran who has been running for years, the chances are that you may have experienced a bit of pain in the knee. This is called runner’s knee. Running is a high-impact activity that puts loads of stress on your knee joints, therefore, increasing the risk of injury and even arthritis. Now, people may assume that running is bad for your knees. This is completely absurd. Running is extremely beneficial for your health. The problem is in the way you run. Running incorrectly is what causes knee and leg pain. If you do it correctly, running doesn’t hurt your knees. People who experience knee and leg pain when running are either doing it incorrectly or have a medical condition that needs to be addressed.

If you have lately experienced knee and lower leg pain after running, then do not take it lightly because it may lead to grave concern in the future if you overlook it today. This is why you are advised to look for the best pain management specialist near me and have your leg and knee diagnosed.

What is a runner’s knee?

Runner’s knee is a condition of the kneecap that emerges when an individual indulges in running activities. It is also known as iliotibial band syndrome, chondromalacia patella, patellofemoral malalignment, and anterior knee syndrome.

Running is an activity that repeatedly stresses the knee joint. Also, this is a common condition in people who are obese or overweight. All the weight and pressure out on the patella make it strain out, causing inflammation and swelling.

The knee and leg pain when running comes in many different forms. It can be dull, sharp, creaky, shocking, zinging, and achy. While knee specialists and physiotherapists use the popular 0-10 scale to measure how much pain affects function, knee, and lower leg pain after running can be very subjective.

For instance, for some people, even a slight ache can be very dreadful when they bend their knee. And for some, they can easily bear the pain while running.
With that said, it is essential to understand the difference between a real injury or an annoying ache.

According to experts, some of the pains and aches associated with running might go away with certain stretches, right hip-strengthening or glutes-quad exercises, or with footwear changes.

However, some aches and pains have serious symptoms and therefore require more attention, which includes pain therapy, physiotherapy, pain medications, rest, and even surgery.

What are the symptoms of knee and leg pain when running?

A dull, aching pain behind or around the kneecap is the primary symptom. This is because when you run, your patella or kneecap meets the lower part of the femur (thighbone).

The pain can be excruciating sometimes, particularly when you:

● Run
● Walk
● Climb or descend stairs
● Sit for a long time with your knees bent

● Sit down and stand up
● Kneel
● Squat

If the condition worsens, you may experience symptoms like grinding or popping in the knee. Please note that the pain can be localized or spread across the knee. So, it is vital that your doctor first determines from where the pain is occurring before beginning the treatment.

To pinpoint the exact location of the injury, the specialist knee doctor will obtain a complete medical history and perform a thorough physical exam, which includes x-rays, CT scans, MRI, or even blood tests.

Treating Severe Knee and Leg Pain

In the majority of the cases, the treatment involves RICE therapy. Following this can give you ample relief from pain. RICE includes:

● REST: avoiding repetitive and constant stress on the injured knee
● ICE: applying ice pack on the injured area for up to 30 minutes
● COMPRESSION: wrapping the injured knee with a medical bandage to restrict swelling
● ELEVATION: placing a pillow under the knee when lying down or sitting to prevent swelling

If you practice this, you will see results within one week. However, if the pain persists and you experience severe knee and leg pain even after the RICE therapy, then your doctor may recommend cold laser therapy.

Cold therapy is the use of a laser of varying wavelengths, also known as low-level laser therapy (LLLT), to enhance the recovery process.

Final Words

If you experience pain in your knee, you should not wait to see how it proceeds and immediately consult your doctor. Getting professional advice will save you both time and money and prevent you from experiencing excruciating pain in the future.

Frequently asked questions

Is it safe to keep running with runner’s knee?
Sometimes, at a reduced level. Pain that stays mild, does not build during the run and settles quickly afterward is often managed by cutting distance, flattening the route and adding strength work. Pain that grows as the run goes on, or that lingers into the next day, is a signal to stop and have the knee examined.

Why would weak hips cause pain at the kneecap?
Because the hip controls how the thigh bone sits beneath the kneecap. When the muscles on the outside of the hip are weak or fatigued, the knee tends to drift inward with each step, changing how the kneecap tracks in its groove and concentrating pressure on one part of the joint surface. That is why hip and glute work is often included.

Does downhill running make kneecap pain worse?
Usually, yes. Running downhill increases the braking load the thigh muscles absorb and the pressure across the kneecap, which is why many runners notice pain on descents first. Surface matters less than most people expect, though repeatedly running on cambered roads and abrupt increases in hills or pace are common triggers.

Does runner’s knee come back once it settles down?
It can, particularly if training load climbs quickly again or the strength work stops. What tends to hold up is a gradual return, keeping hip and thigh strengthening going after the pain has gone, and treating any sudden jump in mileage or intensity as the thing most likely to bring the symptoms back.

posts.title: Does cold laser therapy help for severe neck pain?
posts.excerpt: Today, neck pain is becoming a common condition among the masses, especially the millennials and those who are in their early 50s. The cases of musculoskeletal pain have been on the rise, with people focusing more on their work and careers and less on their health. It is true that a hectic lifestyle filled with […]
posts.content:
Today, neck pain is becoming a common condition among the masses, especially the millennials and those who are in their early 50s. The cases of musculoskeletal pain have been on the rise, with people focusing more on their work and careers and less on their health.

It is true that a hectic lifestyle filled with work and tasks can trigger the occurrence of musculoskeletal pain. It persists when you choose not to do anything about it.

Apart from your packed work schedule, other factors like your posture, your sleeping position, how you sit, any physical activity you, etc. all play a crucial role in how your neck is turning out to be.

According to who, musculoskeletal conditions comprise more than 150 diagnoses that affect the locomotor system.

If you are experiencing severe neck pain, and you have tried all the options out there from OTC medications, physiotherapy, home remedies, etc. then your doctor may prescribe you laser therapy for neck pain. Looking for laser therapy for pain near me can give you the answers you have always been wanting regarding your musculoskeletal health issues.

What Causes Severe Neck Pain ?

Neck pain is one of the most common musculoskeletal conditions that wreak havoc in the lives of nearly 10% of the American population. While the exact cause of severe neck pain is still unknown, given the fact that more than 50% of the American population have degenerative joint disease, the pain can be associated with numerous factors, such as:

● Poor posture
● Cervical nerve root involvement
● Trauma or injury to the neck, such as repetitive occupational injuries or whiplash

If detected and treated early, you can prevent it from becoming chronic. Nevertheless, if the injury is too severe, or there is a failure in the early diagnosis of the pain and injury, it can lead to the following conditions:
● Disc herniations
● A degenerative joint disease of the zygapophyseal joints in the neck
● Degenerative disc disease

Laser Therapy for Neck Pain: How it works?

Pain management laser therapy New York is the latest procedure that comes with several advantages. To start with, laser therapy for pain management use a low wavelength light source in a non-invasive procedure to treat complications in the neck muscle tissues and the related connective tissues. The primary reason why more and more people with musculoskeletal pain prefer laser therapy for neck pain is that it doesn’t require a surgical incision.

It is an outpatient procedure that is conducted at the doctor’s office and usually takes up to 15-20 minutes. There are no pre-procedure preparations; you don’t have to take any medications, nor will you be put under any kind of anesthesia.

The doctor uses a handheld laser device that produces light energy. When it comes in direct contact with your body, the photons emitted by the laser device penetrates your skin to reach the damaged tissue cells.

How Effective is Cold Laser Therapy for Neck Pain?

The effectiveness of cold laser therapy for neck pain can be determined by only after the first couple of treatments. While you will get instant pain relief for that particular day of treatment, to complete pain management, you may have to visit the doctor a couple of times a week or several times in a month.

The procedure only takes 15-20 minutes to complete depending on the severity of the pain and the area being treated. Patients who have undergone laser therapy have spoken highly about the procedure and how it has helped them in combating severe neck pain.

The laser produced by the cold laser machine works to energize the damaging tissue cells. This boosts the recovery process. The process works somewhat similar to photosynthesis. Similar to how plants synthesize the energy of the sunlight to help it grow, the cells synthesize the photons emitted from the light energy.

This triggers cell regeneration, therefore; reducing inflammation and swelling. On the other hand, the cold laser applied to the affected region also numbs the irritating nerves in the area. This lowers the painful sensations you get from moving that particular body part.

Overall, it is the future of musculoskeletal pain management, and coupled with other non-invasive and outpatient procedures like physiotherapy, cryotherapy, acupuncture, etc. cold laser therapy can prove extremely beneficial.

Frequently asked questions

Can cold laser therapy be used when a neck disc is herniated?
It is sometimes included in the plan, but it does not act on the disc itself. Laser is aimed at irritated soft tissue and muscle, so any effect is on the surrounding pain rather than the herniation. Symptoms such as arm weakness, numbness or worsening night pain call for evaluation before starting any modality.

Is laser therapy safe to use over the thyroid?
Providers generally avoid treating directly over the thyroid gland, and over the eyes, as a precaution rather than because harm has been established. The applicator can usually be positioned to treat the neck muscles while staying clear of that area. Anyone with known thyroid disease should mention it so placement can be planned.

Can laser therapy help headaches that start at the base of the skull?
It may, when the headache genuinely originates in the upper neck, since those headaches are driven by irritation in joints and muscles the treatment can reach. Headaches with other causes, including migraine, will not settle simply because the neck was treated. Working out where a headache actually starts is part of the evaluation.

Will neck pain from desk work return after laser therapy ends?
Often, unless what is driving it changes. Treatment can settle the local muscle and tissue irritation, but it does not alter the position the neck holds all day, so workstation setup, movement breaks and strengthening usually have to change alongside it. That is why laser is generally used as one part of a plan rather than on its own.

Neck pain that is not settling on its own?

A physician-led evaluation checks the neck, nerves and posture together. More on neck pain.

posts.title: What are the main causes of knee pain?
posts.excerpt: Knee pain can occur in people of all ages for a variety of reasons. Our knee is a complex part of the body that performs a sophisticated function. Several entities enable the knee to do its job, including the bones, tendons, ligaments, muscles, and cartilage. If any of these parts get damaged or have difficulty […]
posts.content:
Knee pain can occur in people of all ages for a variety of reasons. Our knee is a complex part of the body that performs a sophisticated function. Several entities enable the knee to do its job, including the bones, tendons, ligaments, muscles, and cartilage. If any of these parts get damaged or have difficulty functioning, your knee will suffer. Thus, it is extremely important to perform a thorough check of the knee to determine the cause of severe knee pain.

With a proper diagnosis, it can help the patient relieve symptoms, seek treatment, and regain mobility. Knee pain symptoms will differ from person to person. While two individuals may have the exact same knee problem, but their experience with the pain and symptoms can be different. For instance, some people may be able to tolerate the pain and get on with their daily activities, but others may not be able to move even an inch because of the excruciating pain.

This is why getting yourself diagnosed the moment you feel any discomfort in your knee is important. It starts by analyzing the pain and symptoms. For many, it can be a little overwhelming to distinguish between the symptoms.

This article breaks down the common knee pain symptoms to help you understand the trauma caused to your knee. It also covers the common causes of severe knee pain.

Knee pain symptom checker

The knee pain you experience can be localized to a particular region or spread across the knee. It will vary depending on the structure (bone, ligament, cartilage, tissue, tendon, muscle) involved. If it is an infection, your knee might be completely swollen, and if it is a fracture of a bone or a torn meniscus, the symptoms will only originate from one specific location.

Some of the most common pain include anterior knee pain and sciatic nerve knee pain. While they are common, people don’t know much about their symptoms.

Sciatic nerve knee pain symptoms:

It is not always a physical injury that causes your knee to swell up and make you go through immense pain. The muscles and tissues around your knee are powered by nerves originating in your lower back. Compression or irritation of these nerves at their spinal origin causes symptoms, which may include knee pain.

This condition is known as sciatica. And knee pain may be a symptom of sciatica. The sciatic nerve knee pain symptoms may include:

● Weakness while extending the knee
● Buckling or giving out of the knee
● Inability to bear weight on the knee
● A dull ache, sharp pain, or a warm sensation in the side, front, or back of the knee

The pain can travel through the knee to irritate your calves and ankles.

Symptoms of anterior knee pain:

Anterior knee pain occurs in the front or anterior parts of the knee. It is highly common in women than in men. It can have several causes. For starters, any structural damage to the knee can lead to anterior knee pain. Also, any damage to the cartilage, tendons, ligaments muscles could lead to anterior knee pain.

It is highly common in people who are overweight, those who have suffered any previous injuries to the knee like fracture or dislocation, and those who are athletes or play any sport.

The primary reason why females are more prone to getting anterior knee pain is due to the fact that they have a wider pelvis, which puts more pressure on the knee.

Its symptoms may include:
● Pain when bending the knee
● Difficulty in standing up and sitting down
● Cracking sound of the knee
● Tingling sensation around the knee cup

You have to consult your doctor if you experience any discomfort. Even if there are acute knee pain symptoms, you should get it checked with your primary care physician.

Your doctor may recommend you at-home care treatment like ice packs, compression, elevation, and rest. If you do not feel any relief from pain or discomfort, your doctor may prescribe you to see a specialist like a knee doctor.

Final words

Your knee supports your entire upper body. Thus, it daily undergoes wear and tear, stress, and pressure. Thus, it is important that you keep your knee health in check. Even a little distress can affect the quality of your life.

Frequently asked questions

Can a hip problem cause pain that is felt in the knee?
Yes, and it is easy to miss. Hip arthritis and hip joint irritation commonly refer pain down the front of the thigh to the knee, sometimes with no hip pain at all. A knee that examines and images normally, or that hurts most when turning or getting out of a car, is a reason to have the hip checked as well.

What makes a knee buckle or give way?
Several things can. The thigh muscles can switch off briefly when the joint is painful or swollen, a torn meniscus or loose fragment can catch, a ligament can be unstable after an injury, and nerve irritation from the lower back can weaken the muscles that hold the knee straight. Repeated giving way is worth evaluating rather than bracing and ignoring.

Is a cracking or popping knee something to worry about?
Usually not on its own. Noise from a knee is common and often comes from tendons moving over bone or from gas in the joint fluid. It matters when it arrives with pain, swelling, catching or a sense that the joint locks, which points toward a joint surface or meniscus problem rather than harmless noise.

Does it matter whether a knee swells immediately or the next day?
It can. Swelling within an hour or two of an injury more often means bleeding inside the joint, which raises the possibility of a ligament tear or a fracture. Swelling that builds over the following day is more typical of irritation, a meniscus problem or a flare of arthritis. Either way, the timing is useful information for the examination.

posts.title: How effective is cold laser therapy?
posts.excerpt: Cold laser therapy has become a household name in the United States as an effective pain management procedure for musculoskeletal pain and related diseases such as Low Back Pain, Neck Pain and Knoulders and Knee pain. It is one of the latest procedures in pain management technology. It is the most preferred treatment option for […]
posts.content:
Cold laser therapy has become a household name in the United States as an effective pain management procedure for musculoskeletal pain and related diseases such as Low Back Pain, Neck Pain and Knoulders and Knee pain. It is one of the latest procedures in pain management technology.

It is the most preferred treatment option for those who do not want to go under the knives or take medications. With that said, cold laser therapy has shown promising results in pain relief, particularly for those patients who are seeking treatment without drugs or surgery.

While it doesn’t provide permanent treatment, it plays a crucial role in pain management. Many doctors prescribe cold laser therapy with other noninvasive procedures like physiotherapy, cryotherapy, shockwave therapy, etc. For people treating pain in the joints and muscles.

If you recently started experiencing musculoskeletal pain and were told by your doctor to get cold laser therapy, you may be wondering what it actually is and is it really effective. Well, before you search laser therapy for pain near me, go through this article, which covers everything related to cold laser therapy.

So, without further ado, let’s get started.

What is cold laser therapy?

Cold laser therapy is the use of low-intensity lasers for stimulating the healing process of the cells in the body. It uses low levels of light energy to stimulate connective tissue cells.

Now, most people may be confused with the term ‘cold’ in cold laser therapy. The laser isn’t actually cold, but since extremely low levels of lasers are used, hence, the name.

It is also known as low-level laser therapy (LLLT), photobiomodulation, soft laser biostimulation, and low-power laser therapy (LPLT).

As compared to other forms of lasers used in the medical field, such as those used for correcting the retina, destroying tumors, dissecting brains, and coagulating tissues, the heat dissipated from cold lasers cannot harm you.

How does it work?

The working of a cold laser is similar to photosynthesis. Depending on the severity of musculoskeletal pain you are experiencing, different outputs and wavelengths of low-level light are used. Just like plants use sunlight to heal and develop, our cells are also responsive to light energy, which can increase the process of healing.

For starters, it can be used to treat minor injuries and sprains, including sports injuries. This means injuries like knee pain, lower back pain, neck pain, tennis elbow, bursitis, muscle strains, and ligament sprains can be treated using cold laser therapy.

On the other hand, it also helps in reducing swelling and inflammation, aiding better movement.

The doctor uses a handheld laser device that produces low-level light. It is directly applied to the affected area. The photons emitted from the laser is absorbed by the connective tissue cells. The photons trigger a chemical reaction in the cells, affecting the mitochondria, also known as the powerhouse of the cells. As a result, the damaged cells respond with a psychological reaction. This ultimately promotes cell regeneration.

As said, lasers with different wavelengths are used. For example, for treating superficial tissues, the doctor may use a laser with wavelengths between 600nm and 700nm. In case, if the injury or trauma is deep, a deeper penetration laser will be needed. In that case, the doctor may use wavelengths between 780nm and 950nm.

While you may experience a tingling sensation like the laser is touching your skin, the whole procedure is noninvasive and painless. There will be no or minimal heat or any vibration, and you will not hear any sound as well. Depending on the area that is being treated and how grave the injury is, the laser will be applied from anywhere between 30 seconds to a few several minutes.

Is it effective?

Yes, cold laser therapy is an effective pain management procedure used by doctors. Neuropathic pain to musculoskeletal pain, cold laser therapy is beneficial in providing temporary relief.

And, in the majority of the cases, a single treatment will not work. For the cold laser therapy to be effective, you need at least 3-4 appointments with the doctor in a month. Or several times in a week, depending on how serious the injury or pain is.

Cold laser therapy is approved by the FDA for numerous settings and conditions. When used under the care of a certified practitioner or doctor, cold laser therapy is considered safe.

What are the use cases of cold laser therapy?

Cold laser therapy is highly effective in treating musculoskeletal pain. Whether you are experiencing pain due to old age, due to injury, trauma, or post-surgery, cold laser therapy has many uses in these aspects.

So, search for only the best cold laser therapy near me if you want superior results starting from the first visit.

Frequently asked questions

What does the research say about cold laser therapy for musculoskeletal pain?
Published trials report benefit for several musculoskeletal conditions, with the strongest signal in tendon-related problems and neck and back pain. Study quality and treatment protocols vary considerably, so results are best discussed against a specific diagnosis rather than as a general claim.

How many treatments before cold laser can be judged fairly?
It is a cumulative treatment rather than a single intervention, so a course is usually completed before drawing conclusions. Judging after one or two sessions tends to be premature. The course length is set at assessment and reviewed against the response rather than fixed.

Is cold laser the same as a surgical laser?
No, and the difference is power. Surgical lasers cut or ablate tissue through heat. Cold laser, also called low-level laser therapy or photobiomodulation, uses light at intensities too low to heat tissue, aiming instead to influence cellular activity.

Does cold laser therapy hurt or require recovery time?
Neither, typically. Sessions are painless, sometimes with a mild sensation of warmth, and normal activity resumes immediately. That absence of downtime is one reason it is often used alongside other treatment rather than instead of it.

Wondering whether laser therapy applies to your pain?

A physician-led evaluation finds the driver first, then matches the treatment. More on laser therapy.

posts.title: How does laser therapy work for neuropathic pain?
posts.excerpt: You may have heard people stating they have burning or shooting pain in the hands or feet, or you are experiencing such sensations in your joints. What does this mean? In terms of medical terminology, it is termed neuropathic pain. This is caused by nerve damage that changes the nerve function at the injured area […]
posts.content:
You may have heard people stating they have burning or shooting pain in the hands or feet, or you are experiencing such sensations in your joints. What does this mean? In terms of medical terminology, it is termed neuropathic pain. This is caused by nerve damage that changes the nerve function at the injured area and the region surrounding it.

The experience can be extremely painful. In the majority of the cases, the pain goes on its own, without requiring any serious medical intervention. With some pain therapy and OTC medications, you are good to go. However, if the pain persists or if it is diagnosed a lot later, this can create a lot of problems for you.

The primary reason is that neuropathic pain affects the joints and the surrounding area. So, it can hinder your movement, and thus, compromising your quality of life.

But with the introduction of cold laser therapy, people suffering from neuropathic pain have seen commendable results. If you are someone who has had enough of neuropathic pain, it is high time that you search for cold laser therapy near me because the results are promising.

Keep on reading to know more.

What is Neuropathic Pain?

When your sensory nervous system experiences any disease, trauma, or injury, the nerves within the system fails to work properly, compromising its duty to transmit sensation to the brain. When this happens, the affected area lacks sensation and leads to numbness. However, in other cases, it leads to a sense of pain in the injured region. This is called neuropathic pain, and if left untreated for longer durations, the pain can become unbearable.

It is important to understand that neuropathic pain doesn’t start abruptly, nor it resolves quickly. You will have to let yourself in for dedicated therapy. In extreme cases, you may not be able to move certain body parts, especially if the injury has occurred in the joints. Choosing the right treatment is important because how you lead the rest of your life will completely depend on that.

Most people avoid having surgeries because they can worsen the condition. Pain management with Brooklyn NY laser therapy has emerged as a viable treatment option for patients. Laser therapy for neuropathic pain has shown some incredible results.

What Causes Neuropathic Pain and How Cold Laser Therapy for Neck Pain can Help?

There are numerous reasons why you may develop neuropathic pain in the neck or any other body part. Nevertheless, on a cellular level, it can be because of an increased release of specific neurotransmitters that signals pains, coupled with a disability of nerves to regulate these neurotransmitters can lead to a sensation of pain in the affected region.

In addition to that, in the spinal cord, the cells that are responsible for interpreting painful signals are completely rearranged, which leads to the loss of normally-functioning cell bodies. This leads to a perception of pain, even if the external stimulus is absent. Over time, as the cells continue to perish, the sense of pain increases.

How can laser therapy help?

The best way to treat neuropathy pain is to promote nerve regrowth. While it may seem impossible, medical science has advanced to that phase where nothing seems impossible.

There is one treatment that can prove to be beneficial in the treatment of neuropathic pain. The treatment is called low-level laser therapy (LLLT), and it has been extremely useful in the management of musculoskeletal pain and pain associated with nerve damage.

Light is an essential part of all living things. Based on this simple fact, cold laser therapy was developed. Cold laser therapy uses low wavelengths of light to power the damaged cells and encourages them to regrow.

These lasers produce light energies that are invisible to the naked eye. Since human cells have the ability to absorb and emit light particles, which is called photons, cold laser therapy for neck pain works by locally producing a specific wavelength of light into the targeted cells, or in this case, the actual nerves.

When this happens, the powerhouse of the cells, also known as mitochondria, absorbs the light energy and is triggered to work faster. This increases the recovery in the cells of the nerves.

How long does the procedure take?

It depends on the severity of your condition, the wavelength of the laser used, and the area being treated. Nonetheless, it may easily take up to 3-4 visits to the doctor to complete the therapy. When looking for cold laser therapy near me, always choose a certified clinic.

Frequently asked questions

Why does nerve pain respond differently from muscle pain?
Because the mechanism differs. Muscle pain reflects tissue that is strained or overloaded and settles as that resolves. Nerve pain comes from damaged or irritated nerve fibers signaling incorrectly, so it can persist without any ongoing tissue damage and often does not respond to treatments aimed at muscle.

How might laser therapy affect an irritated nerve?
Published research describes effects on cellular energy production, local circulation and inflammatory signaling in treated tissue, all of which influence how a nerve behaves. It is a supporting intervention rather than a repair mechanism, and the evidence is stronger for some nerve conditions than others.

Is laser therapy used on its own for nerve pain?
Rarely. Nerve pain usually has a driver, whether compression, a metabolic cause such as diabetes, or a vitamin deficiency, and treating the symptom without addressing that limits results. Laser is generally one component alongside work on the underlying cause.

Which kinds of nerve pain are least likely to respond?
Nerve pain from significant structural compression tends to need the compression addressed first. Long-standing damage with substantial fiber loss also responds less readily than recent irritation. Both are identified at assessment, which is why realistic expectations are set before a course starts.

Nerve pain that has not responded to anything yet?

A physician-led evaluation looks for the driver before treating the symptom. More on peripheral neuropathy.

posts.title: How can laser therapy help to get rid of acute back pain?
posts.excerpt: Back pain is quite common in humans, irrespective of their age and gender. Acute back pain can occur due to numerous reasons, like lifting weights, improper posture, and even living a sedentary lifestyle can lead to back pain, among other things. Acute back pain is tolerable if it only lasts for a couple of days. […]
posts.content:
Back pain is quite common in humans, irrespective of their age and gender. Acute back pain can occur due to numerous reasons, like lifting weights, improper posture, and even living a sedentary lifestyle can lead to back pain, among other things.

Acute back pain is tolerable if it only lasts for a couple of days. If it prolongs, the pain can interfere with your day-to-day life, making it an uncomfortable and painful experience. Thus, laser therapy for back pain can help in this instance. Unlike other types of back pain management and treatment, laser therapy is a non-invasive procedure that usually takes 15-20 minutes to complete. How the invasive and non-invasive routes compare directly is set out in comparing invasive and non-invasive pain relief.

Before you search for laser therapy near me, it is important that you know how it works and how it can help you get rid of acute back pain. With that said, this post covers what you need to know about cold laser therapy for back pain.

Let’s jump right into it.

The Concept of Laser in Pain Management

The use of lasers in medical intervention is not new. Previously, the laser has been used for numerous surgical procedures, mostly to remove or dissect parts. However, the concept of cold laser therapy is quite new. The idea is that light energy produced by medical equipment penetrates your skin and dives into the tissues to reduce inflammation and pain. Specific wavelengths of the laser are used for the therapy. It is also known as low-level laser therapy (LLLT), which uses a non-invasive light source to generate a single wavelength of light.

What’s unique about this laser is that it doesn’t produce any sound, heat, or vibration. It is designed in a way that the light energy penetrates through the skin and affects the function of the connective tissues; therefore, accelerating the recovery of damaged tissue cells.

Since it accelerates the healing process, it can be used for treating chronic and acute musculoskeletal pain, including back pain.

That is, laser therapy for back pain can help you eliminate swelling, pain, and reduce muscle spasms to increase functionality.

How Laser Therapy for Back Pain Work

You may have to visit the laser therapy clinic in Brooklyn, NY multiple times to get the treatment done. It takes multiple procedures to treat damaged tissue cells.

The laser is applied directly over the affected back where you feel the most pain. The laser will be placed over the area for 2-5 minutes, depending on the severity of the pain, discomfort, and the size of the area being treated. Moreover, the duration for which the laser will be focused on your back will also depend on the wavelength at which the laser is used.

The laser may be placed and removed several times on your injured back for 15-20 minutes. During this time, the laser produces non-thermal photons of light that pass through the skin layers to reach the connective tissues. The light energy can easily penetrate 2-5cm underneath the skin without making you feel anything.

Once the light energy reaches the affected region, it is absorbed into the tissue cells and interacts with the light-sensitive elements in the cells. To better understand how cold therapy works for your back, consider photosynthesis in plants. The plants absorb sunlight and then convert it into usable energy, making the plant grow. Its application to back pain in particular is covered in how cryotherapy is changing back pain management.

Similarly, when the cells in your injured back tissues absorb the light energy produced by the laser, it activates the cell’s natural process of regeneration; therefore, normalizing the injured or damaged tissue.

You will feel a significant reduction in pain and inflammation after the first treatment itself. The light energy boosts the healing time, allowing your injured back muscles to regenerate quickly.

While you may feel instant pain relief, the effect will wear off after a couple of hours. This is why multiple treatments are required within a week’s or month’s time.

Certain low-level laser therapy devices are FDA approved, making them perfect for pain management.

Frequently asked questions

Is cold laser therapy safe during pregnancy?
Treatment over the abdomen and lower back is generally avoided in pregnancy, because the effects there have not been established. That is a precaution rather than evidence of harm, and other areas may still be treatable. Anyone who is pregnant or trying to conceive should say so before a course of laser therapy is planned.

Does a tattoo or darker skin affect laser therapy?
It can affect how the treatment is delivered. Darker pigment and tattoo ink absorb more light energy, which means more of it becomes heat at the skin rather than passing through, so providers often reduce intensity or adjust placement over tattooed areas. Mentioning tattoos in the treatment area beforehand is worth doing.

Does an acute back flare need to settle before starting laser therapy?
Usually not, which is one reason it gets considered early. Treatment involves lying still rather than moving the painful area, and the handpiece is held over the skin rather than pressed in like manual therapy. Position can be adjusted for comfort, though an examination still comes first to establish what is driving the flare.

Is laser applied to bare skin or through clothing?
Directly on bare skin in almost all cases. Fabric scatters and absorbs the light before it reaches tissue, so the treatment area is exposed and the handpiece is held against or just above the skin. Sessions are short, and only the area being treated needs to be uncovered.

Back pain that keeps coming back?

An evaluation looks at what maintains the problem, not just what triggered it. More on lower back pain.

posts.title: Why does my knee still hurt 6 months after surgery?
posts.excerpt: This is a question asked by many patients who have undergone knee surgery and still haven’t found any relief. Recovery from surgery can take several months, and if you have soreness, inflammation, or swelling in the treated area, it is not unusual. This can be because of edema, which is a psychological response to a […]
posts.content:
This is a question asked by many patients who have undergone knee surgery and still haven’t found any relief. Recovery from surgery can take several months, and if you have soreness, inflammation, or swelling in the treated area, it is not unusual. This can be because of edema, which is a psychological response to a chemical imbalance within the tissues and cells of the body. Surgical interventions can put a lot of mechanical stress on the tissue.

Knee replacement is a commonly performed orthopedic surgical procedure. It is done when the knee joints are worn out as a result of arthritis. The orthopedic doctor for knee pain removes the worn-out cartilage and shapes the ends of the bone. Then a metal implant is fit over the ends of the bone, and a plastic spacer is inserted between the metal implants. Deciding whether the next appointment should be with a surgeon is the subject of when to see a knee orthopedic doctor.

While the surgery may be a success, in order to allow a smooth and pain-free movement of the knee joint, the patient has to go through rehabilitation and therapy. This is because your body is getting accustomed to the artificial part, and it will need some time to accept the implant.

On the other hand, there are chances that even after the completion of rehabilitation, the patient may feel immense pain or any discomfort in the knee. The specialist doctor for knee pain suggests that the reasons for dissatisfaction are obvious – bone fracture around the replacement, postoperative infection, or pain around the newly replaced joint. As per the Bone & Joint Journal, up to 20% of patients are not satisfied with the outcome following total knee replacement.

Before you search the best doctor for knee pain near me, it is important that you understand the root cause of the pain even after 6 months of surgery. This is extremely important as you would want yourself to be aware of things regarding the surgery before you get any other medical attention.

What causes knee pain even after 6 months of surgery?

The pain management doctors in Brooklyn New York, say that the primary step in finding a solution to constant knee pain is to first identify the cause of pain. Without knowing what is causing the pain, it is extremely difficult to pitch a suitable treatment. With that said, here are the most common causes of persistent knee pain after surgery.

  • Alignment Problems: A poorly aligned knee implant may not function well, irrespective of its brand. A defective implant can cause some serious damage to the treated knee. This can be because of a manufacturing error or an error in computer navigation.
  • Kneecap Problems: Kneecap or patellofemoral problems are one of the common reasons causing pain after knee surgery. During rehabilitation or in your day to day activities, any body movement that requires the use of the knee puts significant pressure on the kneecap.
  • Infection: An infection in the operated knee is a worrisome concern. If you feel increased pain most often, it could be a sign of an infection. It is important to diagnose the symptoms early on because delay in treatment can be technically challenging, even for a skilled surgeon.
  • Loosening of the Implant: If the implant is not properly fitted, it may lose its hold on the bones. This can cause severe pain. On the other hand, over the years, the implant tends to lose its hold on the bones. This is often the primary cause of pain, years or decades after the surgery.

What are the common diagnostic signs?

The doctor for knee pain will take several steps to examine your pain. He/she will talk to you and discuss the pain. How you describe your knee pain will help the doctor for pain management in New York in making an accurate diagnosis.

It is common to experience start-up pain (pain while rising), and it usually goes away within a few months after surgery. If you experience any other type of pain, it is possible that you have a more serious condition. The doctor will try to find the exact location of the pain and the timing as well to pinpoint the underlying cause. The following are some common diagnostic signs that you should know:

  • A deformed knee indicates a patellofemoral problem
  • Pain accompanied by fever, redness, and swelling indicates infection
  • A sudden appearance of pain could be a sign of injury or fracture
  • Pain while using stairs suggest a kneecap issue
  • Persistent start-up pain could be a sign of a misaligned implant or a loosening implant

Treatment

Low-Level Laser Therapy or LLLT is a proven method for pain management and tissue repair after knee surgery. It can be used alongside physical therapy to curb the pain.

The light energy produced triggers cell regeneration, thereby boosting the healing process. But you should know that while it is a non-invasive procedure, you will have to make several appointments with the pain management doctors in Brooklyn, New York before you can finally see the results. It is only a temporary solution, but it will help reduce the pain while your body heals.

Frequently asked questions

Is it normal for a replaced knee to feel warm months after surgery?
Mild warmth and puffiness can persist for a year or more while the joint settles, especially after a busy day. What changes the picture is warmth that increases rather than fades, redness that spreads, fever, or new pain at rest, since that combination points toward infection and calls for prompt assessment rather than watchful waiting.

Can scar tissue inside the knee cause lasting stiffness?
Yes. Excess scar tissue forming inside the joint, sometimes called arthrofibrosis, can limit how far the knee bends or straightens and make movement painful at the end of the range. It is one reason persistent stiffness is assessed differently from persistent pain, because the options that follow, including targeted therapy or a further procedure, are different.

Does clicking from a knee replacement mean the implant is loose?
Not by itself. Metal and plastic bearing surfaces commonly produce audible clicks, particularly when standing up or using stairs, and many people hear them for years without any problem. Clicking that appears alongside new pain, a sense of instability, or a change in how the leg lines up is the combination that warrants imaging.

How is an infected knee replacement tested for?
Usually with a combination of tests. Blood markers of inflammation are a starting point, and fluid taken from the joint can be sent for cell counts and culture, which is often the more informative step. Imaging may be added to look at the bone around the implant. Suspected infection is investigated promptly rather than watched.

Related: knee injections in Brooklyn are a non-surgical, drug-free option for knee osteoarthritis pain.

posts.title: Joint Lubricant (Gel) Injections for Knee Pain: How They Work, Cost and What to Expect
posts.excerpt: People diagnosed with knee osteoarthritis are prescribed with treatment options like physical therapy and medications. However, in some cases, these options fail to provide relief from pain and stiffness.
posts.content:
TL;DR

Joint lubricant injections, also called gel, hyaluronic acid (HA) or viscosupplement injections, add a thick lubricating fluid to a knee with osteoarthritis.

  • They can ease pain and stiffness for some people, usually starting within a few weeks and lasting up to about six months.
  • They do not rebuild cartilage or cure arthritis, and results vary. Medical guidelines are mixed on how much they help.
  • Some products are a single shot; others are a series of 3 to 5 weekly shots.
  • Medicare and many New York Medicaid plans cover them for knee osteoarthritis when criteria are met.
  • They work best alongside exercise, physical therapy and weight management.

What are joint lubricant injections?

Joint lubricant injections put hyaluronic acid, a gel-like substance, into the knee joint. Hyaluronic acid occurs naturally in healthy joint fluid, where it helps the joint glide and absorb shock. In knee osteoarthritis, the joint fluid becomes thinner and less cushioning. The injection supplements that fluid, which is why it is also called viscosupplementation.

You may hear them called: – Gel injections or knee gel shots – Hyaluronic acid (HA) injections – Viscosupplement injections – Brand names such as Synvisc-One, Euflexxa, Durolane, Monovisc, Gel-One, Orthovisc or Hyalgan

What lubricates the knee joint naturally?

Synovial fluid lubricates the knee. It is made by the lining of the joint and contains hyaluronic acid, which gives it a slippery, gel-like texture. Movement circulates this fluid and helps nourish cartilage, which has no blood supply of its own. That is one reason regular, gentle movement matters so much for arthritic knees.

How can you keep your knee joints lubricated without an injection?

You cannot add fluid to the knee by eating or drinking something, but you can help the joint work better: – Move often. Walking, cycling and water exercise keep joint fluid circulating. See aqua therapy. – Strengthen the thigh and hip muscles to take load off the joint. See physical therapy. – Lose extra weight if you carry it; every pound adds several pounds of force to the knee with each step. – Warm up stiff knees with heat or a few minutes of easy movement before activity. – Be cautious with supplements. Major arthritis guidelines do not recommend glucosamine or chondroitin for knee osteoarthritis because the evidence is weak.

Who are joint lubricant injections for?

They are mainly used for knee osteoarthritis that still hurts after basic treatments. A doctor may suggest them if you: – Have knee osteoarthritis confirmed by exam and X-ray – Still have pain despite exercise, physical therapy, weight management or pain relievers – Cannot take anti-inflammatory medicines, or they do not help enough – Want to delay knee replacement or are not ready for surgery

They are not designed for knee pain from a ligament tear, a locked knee, or pain coming from the hip or lower back. See what doctor to see for knee pain.

Do knee gel injections work?

They help some people and not others. Studies show modest average benefit, and some people get several months of meaningful relief while others notice little change.

What the guidelines say (honest version): – The American College of Rheumatology and Arthritis Foundation (2019) conditionally recommend against routine use for knee osteoarthritis because the average benefit in studies is small. – The American Academy of Orthopaedic Surgeons (2021) does not recommend routine use. – In practice, many doctors still offer them to selected patients who have not done well with other treatments, and Medicare covers them under set criteria.

The bottom line: they are an option to discuss, not a guaranteed fix, and they work best as part of a full plan. See knee osteoarthritis: non-surgical options.

How many gel injections do you need: one shot or a series?

It depends on the product. Some are given as a single injection; others as a series:

Type Typical schedule Examples
Single injection 1 shot Synvisc-One, Durolane, Monovisc, Gel-One
Short series 3 shots, one week apart Euflexxa, Orthovisc (3 to 4)
Longer series 5 shots, one week apart Hyalgan, Supartz

Your doctor and your insurance plan usually decide which product is used. Neither type has been shown to be clearly better than the other.

How long do joint lubricant injections last?

Relief, when it happens, usually starts within 2 to 5 weeks and can last up to about six months. A course can be repeated if it helped; Medicare generally allows a repeat course no sooner than six months after the last one.

What happens during a gel injection?

The injection is done in the office and takes a few minutes: 1. The skin is cleaned and may be numbed. 2. If the knee is swollen, extra fluid may be drawn out first. 3. The gel is injected into the joint, sometimes with ultrasound guidance for accuracy. See ultrasound-guided injections. 4. You can usually walk out and return to normal light activity the same day.

Most doctors advise avoiding heavy exercise, long standing and heavy lifting for about 48 hours.

What are the side effects of knee gel injections?

Most side effects are mild and short-lived: – Pain, warmth or swelling in the knee for a day or two – Mild stiffness or a feeling of fullness

Less common: a flare of swelling and pain lasting a few days. Rare but serious: infection. Call your doctor promptly if the knee becomes hot, red and very painful, or if you develop a fever.

Who should not get gel injections?

You may not be a candidate if you have: – An infection in or near the knee – A skin condition at the injection site – An allergy to hyaluronic acid products; some products are made from rooster combs, so tell your doctor about any allergy to birds, feathers or egg products – Knee pain from a cause other than osteoarthritis

Tell your doctor if you take blood thinners.

How much do knee gel injections cost, and does insurance cover them?

Cost depends mostly on your insurance. Medicare Part B covers hyaluronic acid injections for knee osteoarthritis when medical criteria are met, such as confirmed osteoarthritis and other treatments tried first. Many New York Medicaid managed care plans, including Healthfirst, Fidelis Care and MetroPlusHealth, also cover them, sometimes with prior authorization. Without insurance, the product alone can cost several hundred dollars or more per course, so check coverage before your visit. See does Medicare cover pain management and does Medicaid cover pain-management injections.

Gel injection or cortisone shot: what is the difference?

They do different jobs. A cortisone (steroid) injection reduces inflammation and often works within days, but relief usually lasts weeks to a few months. A gel injection supplements joint fluid; relief, when it comes, builds over weeks and may last longer. Doctors sometimes use cortisone for a flare and consider gel when pain keeps returning. See steroid injections and how often you can get a cortisone shot.

Can gel injections help you avoid knee replacement?

There is no proof they prevent knee replacement, but for some people they ease pain enough to stay active and delay surgery. The strongest tools for delaying replacement are exercise and weight management. See how to avoid or delay knee replacement.

Frequently asked questions

Is a gel injection the same as lubricant injected into the knee?

Yes. “Joint lubricant injection” and “gel injection” usually mean the same thing: hyaluronic acid injected into the knee.

Do gel injections hurt?

Most people feel brief pressure or a sting. The skin is often numbed first, and the injection takes a few minutes.

Can I walk after a knee gel injection?

Yes. Most people walk out normally. Avoid strenuous activity for about 48 hours.

Can you get gel injections in other joints?

They are approved mainly for the knee. Use in other joints, such as the hip or shoulder, is less established; ask your doctor.

How soon will I feel a difference?

Usually within 2 to 5 weeks, if the injection helps.

What if the first gel injection did not help?

If one course did not help, another usually is not repeated. Your doctor may suggest other options.

Are gel injections safe if I have diabetes?

Generally yes, and unlike cortisone they do not usually raise blood sugar. Tell your doctor about your diabetes before treatment.

Where can I get hyaluronic acid injections?

They are offered by pain management, orthopedic, physical medicine and some rheumatology practices. Check that the provider is in network for your plan.

Take the next step

If knee arthritis pain keeps coming back, an evaluation can show whether gel injections, another treatment or a combination makes sense for you. See HA knee injections, knee pain and what to expect at your first visit.

posts.title: How to Avoid or Delay Knee Replacement: What Actually Helps
posts.excerpt: TL;DR Many people with knee osteoarthritis delay knee replacement for years, and some never need it. The steps with the strongest evidence are simple, but they take consistency. Exercise and physical therapy to strengthen the thigh and hip muscles are the most proven non-surgical treatments. Weight loss reduces the load on the knee with every […]
posts.content:
TL;DR

Many people with knee osteoarthritis delay knee replacement for years, and some never need it. The steps with the strongest evidence are simple, but they take consistency.

  • Exercise and physical therapy to strengthen the thigh and hip muscles are the most proven non-surgical treatments.
  • Weight loss reduces the load on the knee with every step.
  • Pain relief (topical or oral anti-inflammatories, steroid injections) helps you stay active.
  • Gel injections and newer therapies help some people; results vary.
  • Replacement is worth considering when pain limits daily life despite months of good non-surgical care.

Can you avoid knee replacement?

Often you can delay it, and sometimes avoid it. Knee replacement is usually recommended for advanced osteoarthritis that keeps limiting walking, sleep and daily activities despite non-surgical treatment. Arthritis does not progress at the same speed in everyone, and many people manage their symptoms for years. Nobody can promise a knee will never need surgery, but the steps below give you the best chance. See knee osteoarthritis: symptoms and stages.

Which exercises help you avoid knee replacement?

Strengthening exercises are the most proven non-surgical treatment for knee arthritis. Strong quadriceps (front of the thigh) and hip muscles take pressure off the joint. Helpful options include: – Straight-leg raises and seated leg extensions – Sit-to-stand from a chair – Side-lying hip raises and glute bridges – Low-impact cardio: walking, stationary cycling, water exercise

A physical therapist can build a plan that matches your pain level and progress it safely. See physical therapy and aqua therapy.

How much does weight loss help the knee?

A lot. Each pound of body weight puts several pounds of force through the knee with every step. For people with extra weight, losing even 5 to 10 percent of body weight can noticeably reduce knee pain and improve function. Weight loss works best combined with exercise.

What pain treatments help you stay active?

Pain control matters because it lets you keep moving. Options include: – Topical anti-inflammatory gels on the knee – Oral anti-inflammatories, if your doctor says they are safe for you – Steroid (cortisone) injections for flare-ups; relief usually lasts weeks to a few months. See steroid injections and how often you can get a cortisone shot. – A cane in the hand opposite the painful knee, or a knee brace for support

Do gel (hyaluronic acid) injections prevent knee replacement?

There is no proof that gel injections prevent knee replacement, but some people get months of pain relief from them. Medical guidelines are mixed: some do not recommend them routinely, while others see a place for them in selected patients. If you are considering them, ask about your expected benefit and cost. See HA knee injections and gel knee injections: cost and what to expect.

What about shockwave, laser and other newer therapies?

Technology-based therapies such as shockwave, laser and TECAR are used to ease knee pain and support rehab. Research is still developing, and they work best as part of a plan that includes exercise. See shockwave therapy and knee pain treatment without surgery.

What daily habits protect your knees?

  • Keep moving through the day; long sitting stiffens arthritic knees
  • Choose supportive, cushioned shoes
  • Use rails on stairs and avoid deep squats and kneeling during flares
  • Use heat for stiffness and ice for swelling
  • Manage blood sugar if you have diabetes, since it affects joints and healing

When is knee replacement the right choice?

Knee replacement is worth discussing when severe pain and stiffness keep limiting walking, sleep or daily tasks despite several months of consistent non-surgical care, and X-rays show advanced arthritis. It is a highly successful surgery for the right patient. Choosing it is not a failure; it is a decision about quality of life. If you still have pain after a replacement, see why do I still have pain after knee replacement? (publishes Jan 4).

Frequently asked questions

Can you reverse knee arthritis?

Cartilage loss cannot be reversed, but pain and function often improve a lot with exercise, weight loss and treatment.

At what age do most people get a knee replacement?

Most knee replacements are done in people in their 60s and 70s, but age matters less than symptoms and X-ray findings.

Is walking good for knees with arthritis?

Yes, for most people. Regular, comfortable walking keeps the joint moving and the muscles strong. Shorten the distance during flares.

Can a knee brace help me avoid surgery?

A brace can reduce pain and improve stability for some people, which helps them stay active. It does not stop arthritis.

How long can you delay a knee replacement?

It varies. Some people delay it for years with good non-surgical care; others reach the point where surgery makes sense sooner.

Does insurance cover non-surgical knee treatment?

Most plans cover physical therapy and injections, sometimes with prior authorization. Check with your plan. See [does Medicare cover pain management](https://paintherapycare.com/blog/medicare-pain-management-brooklyn/).

Take the next step

If knee arthritis is slowing you down, a non-surgical plan can start now. See what to expect at your first visit and knee pain.
